content.title: Andreas Rödder: «The pendulum is swinging to the right»
content.lead: Historian Andreas Rödder sees Germany facing a «paradigm shift of the political system.» The AfD is polling at around 30%. For Rödder, the question therefore arises whether The Union can catch the «pendulum» in the right-wing center.

videos.title: Andreas Rödder: «The pendulum is swinging to the right»
videos.description: Historian Andreas Rödder sees Germany facing a «paradigm shift in its political system.» The AfD is polling at around 30 percent. For Rödder, the question therefore is whether the CDU/CSU can catch the «pendulum» in the center-right.
videos.author: Nick Bauhan

videos.title: Holger Friedrich: «We need a completely new vision»
videos.description: The entrepreneur and publisher discusses social division and the question of how Germany can come together more strongly again.
videos.author: Nick Bauhan

videos.title: Holger Friedrich: «If I were a young person, I would withdraw from Germany.»
videos.description: In the podcast «NZZ Machtspiel», the entrepreneur and publisher talks about Germany's economic prospects, wealth accumulation and why he recommends that young people look beyond national borders.
videos.author: Nick Bauhan

videos.title: Protests by ultra-Orthodox Jews outside a café in Jerusalem
videos.description: For several weeks, ultra-Orthodox Jews have been protesting in front of a café in Jerusalem. The reason is that it is open on Shabbat. The café can now only open under heavy police protection. Johannes C. Bockenheimer was on site and spoke with the owner.

videos.title: «The boundaries of what can be said must be broad,» says Harald Martenstein
videos.description: In «NZZ Machtspiel,» writer and columnist Harald Martenstein spoke about cancel culture and free speech. He never felt canceled.

metadata.title: «Are you saving democracy with provocation, Harald Martenstein?»

teaserImage.teaserCaption: The AfD's platform? It has «a Helmut Kohl whiff» about it. The «Bild» newspaper? A «new universe.» Columnist Harald Martenstein explains in the podcast «Power Play» why he doesn't feel canceled and where Angela Merkel was more sovereign than Friedrich Merz.

metadata.seoTitle: Can democracy be saved through provocation? A conversation with Harald Martenstein.
metadata.seoDescription: Martenstein discusses a potential ban on the AfD, the limits of what can be said, and the state of democratic debate in Germany. He defends his speech in the "Trial Against Germany" and warns of the political consequences of banning the party.
metadata.seoSocialMediaTitle: In the NZZ podcast: Martenstein on the AfD, Helmut Schmidt and right-wing politics
metadata.paywallQuestionOne: How does Harald Martenstein assess the attempts to ban the AfD?
metadata.paywallQuestionTwo: Why does Martenstein see Helmut Schmidt rather than Hitler in AfD voters?
metadata.paywallQuestionThree: Is Martenstein anticipating a moral and political backlash from the right?
metadata.nzzArticleSnippet: Das AfD-Programm? Hat «einen Helmut-Kohl-Geruch». Die «Bild»-Zeitung? Ein «neues Universum». Der Kolumnist Harald Martenstein erklärt im Podcast «Machtspiel», wieso er sich nicht gecancelt fühlt und wo Angela Merkel souveräner war als Friedrich Merz.
metadata.teaserCaption: The AfD's platform? It has «a Helmut Kohl whiff» about it. The «Bild» newspaper? A «new universe.» Columnist Harald Martenstein explains in the podcast «Power Play» why he doesn't feel canceled and where Angela Merkel was more sovereign than Friedrich Merz.
metadata.leadText: The AfD's platform? It has «a Helmut Kohl whiff» about it. The «Bild» newspaper? A «new universe.» Columnist Harald Martenstein explains in the podcast «Power Play» why he doesn't feel canceled and where Angela Merkel was more sovereign than Friedrich Merz.
metadata.nzzSummaryEN:
• Harald Martenstein criticizes the proposed ban of the AfD in a theater play, emphasizing its significance due to the party's broad support.
• According to Martenstein, AfD voters seek leadership akin to Helmut Schmidt's, focused on stability and practical problem-solving, not extremist approaches.
• In the podcast, he also discusses his work at BILD and the current political dynamics in Germany.
metadata.nzzSummaryDE:
• In a play, Harald Martenstein criticizes the planned ban on the AfD and emphasizes its importance in view of the party's broad support.
 • According to Martenstein, AfD voters are looking for a leadership style similar to that of Helmut Schmidt, which stands for stability and problem-solving, not extremist approaches.
 • In the podcast he also talks about his work at BILD and the current political dynamics in Germany.
